title: `notifications/tools/list_changed`
description: The notification a server sends when its tool list changes, delivered on a subscription stream the client opted into with `toolsListChanged`.
question: Does the framework refresh its tool list when the server says it changed?
why: Adapters cache the tool list at startup. Without this, an agent keeps offering tools the server has withdrawn and never sees the ones it added, and the mismatch only shows up as a failed call much later.
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers publishing this. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.

notes.genkit_js: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: no handler for `notifications/tools/list_changed` is registered and there is no change hook; each `getActiveTools` call lists again, so a caller that re-lists sees the added tool.
notes.mastra: Mastra 2.2.0 against a 2025-11-25 server: `onListChanged('src', fn)` installs the handler, and it fired and the next list showed the change. But the call itself rejects with `subscriptions/listen needs MCP 2026-07-28`, because it also tries to open a 2026-07-28 stream. Code that awaits the registration sees an error for a hook that works.
notes.crewai: CrewAI 1.15.26: `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` takes no message handler or callback, and its `tools` property returns the list it built at start. After the fixture added a tool and fired the notification, a crew was still handed the old list.
notes.google_adk: Google ADK 2.11.0: `McpToolset` takes no message handler, so nothing an application registers hears the notification. `get_tools` relists on every call by default (`tool_list_cache_ttl_seconds=None`), so the next list showed the added tool anyway. ADK documents that with `tool_list_cache_ttl_seconds` set, a change goes unnoticed until the cache entry expires.
notes.autogen: AutoGen 0.7.5: The workbench registers no message handler, so no hook hears the notification; its `list_tools` asks the server every time, so the next listing shows the change.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): MCPClient registers no notification handler: a server notification reaches only `onUncaughtError`, as an "Unsupported message type" error that does not name the notification. `client.tools()` lists again on every call, so the next call shows the added tool.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the SDK takes no notification handler, so `notifications/tools/list_changed` reaches nothing. `cacheToolsList` defaults to false, so the next `listTools` (and the next agent turn) asks the server again and shows the change.
notes.semantic_kernel: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: the default `message_handler` awaits `load_tools()` inside the MCP session's receive loop. Its `tools/list` reply cannot be read until the request times out (30 s here, never with the default `request_timeout=None`), so the call that triggered the change fails and the list stays stale.
notes.llamaindex: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `BasicMCPClient` takes no message handler and closes its session after every call (over stdio it also starts a fresh server process per call), so no session is open to hear `notifications/tools/list_changed`, and the next `McpToolSpec` listing did not show the added tool.
notes.google_adk_js: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPToolset` opens a new session for every operation (`getTools`, `listResources`, `readResource`, each tool call) and closes it after; over stdio that is a new server process each time. No session outlives the call that changed the list, and over stdio the added tool dies with its process, so the next `getTools` matched the one before.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` registers no message handler, so no hook hears the notification. `build_tools` lists again, so the next build shows the change, but an `Agent` calls it per run only with `refresh_connection=True`.
notes.haystack: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPClient` builds its `ClientSession` with no message handler, and `MCPToolset.warm_up` lists tools once and returns early after that, so `notifications/tools/list_changed` reaches nothing and the toolset keeps its first list.
notes.smolagents: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): mcpadapt opens its `ClientSession` with no message handler, and `MCPClient.get_tools()` returns the list built at connect and never relists. After the fixture added a tool and fired the notification, the agent was still handed the old list.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy has no notification hook and no relist. The change shows only when the caller lists again on its session and converts each tool with `from_mcp_tool` again.
notes.beeai: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: no notification hook and no relist. Calling `MCPTool.from_client` again on the same session shows the change, so the caller has to know when to.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient` builds its `ClientSession` with no message handler and has no list-changed hook, and `Agent(mcps=...)` resolves the tool list once, so `notifications/tools/list_changed` goes unseen and the agent keeps the stale list.
notes.google_adk_java: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: The adapter registers no `toolsChangeConsumer` consumer, so nothing tells the agent the list changed. The next `McpToolset.getTools` call (or session `listTools`) lists again and shows the change.
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: `fromClient` lists tools once into a fixed `ToolRegistry` and registers no `notifications/tools/list_changed` handler, so the agent keeps the stale list. A new `fromClient` call on the same `Client` would list again.
